bull_bear.body:
- **Net debt INR686 cr** (up YoY from 653.1); leverage ~3.75x.
- Scheduled repayments **~INR110–120 cr/yr over next 3 years** — "downward gliding path."
- Working capital sharply improved (7 days vs 33). No dividend commentary on this call.
- Potential land sale as deleveraging / shareholder-reward catalyst.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Net debt elevated** (~3.75x); deleveraging dependent on EBITDA growth + scheduled repayments (and possibly land sale).
- **RM lag recovery uncertain** — INR19 cr FY26 loss recovery only "parallelly going on," not booked.
- **Aggressive FY27 guidance** (>INR3,000 cr / ~21%+) vs OEM industry growth of 5–8% — relies on ~40 launches ramping on schedule (execution/launch-timing risk).
- **Execution slippage track record** — Railways/Defence FY26 missed prior INR60–70 cr guidance due to approval delays.
- OEM/customer concentration; commodity (aluminium) and FX (INR) cost inflation.
- EV transition pace — Hosur tied to hybrid/EV ramp at OEMs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and candid. Transparent on one-off bridge (reported 9% → normalized 10.25%) and on the structural fix (monthly RM settlement, 75% agreed). Honest admission that FY26 Railways/Defence targets were missed on approval delays. Concrete numbers on order book, capex, leverage. Slight internal inconsistency on Q4 adjusted margin (9.5% vs 9.8%). Forward export/growth claims are bold and worth tracking against delivery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Reported margin understates true profitability by ~125 bps (9.0% → 10.25%); FY27 starts from a cleaner, higher base from Q1.
- Growth is **structural/share-gain + single-source new programs**, not cyclical OEM volume — decoupled from the modest 5–8% industry growth.
- **Railways is the near-term surprise lever** (INR3–4 cr → INR100 cr target, higher margin, minimal capex on existing capacity).
- **Land monetization** (>INR700 cr rejected; mkt cap context relevant) is a potentially large, under-appreciated balance-sheet/shareholder catalyst.
- CNC machine-tool external sales = new, optional revenue stream.
- Despite "EV-agnostic" framing, EV is still pipeline-only — no current EV revenue disclosure; Hosur is the EV/hybrid proof point.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing relationships with global automotive OEMs - BMW, Hero, Maruti Suzuki, Toyota, Renault, Nissan, Tata Motors, Cummins, Honda, Mahindra, Volvo and Bajaj
- Integrated 'concept to delivery' capability spanning product design, tooling, casting (aluminium and ferrous), precision machining and assembly
- Strong in-house R&D, design, development and engineering services, testing and validation, and special purpose machines with CNC controls
- Powertrain-agnostic portfolio supporting Hybrid, Electric and Internal Combustion Engine applications
- 16 geographically spread manufacturing plants, strategically located to de-risk operations
- Export franchise across 8 countries supported by warehousing in Europe (Germany, France) and USA (Detroit, North Carolina, Ohio) and business representation across key global markets
- Customer pass-through mechanism for raw-material cost: volatile aluminium and other raw material prices were managed with limited effect on margins
- CRISIL A/Stable long-term and CRISIL A1 short-term ratings on bank facilities, assigned on a consolidated view of the Company and its subsidiaries
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Complex, fast-changing operating environment across manufacturing and distribution — MD&A Risks & Concerns: evolving market conditions, global supply chain interdependencies, changing customer expectations, stringent regulatory requirements and operational risks across the manufacturing and distribution network; macroeconomic developments, geopolitical events, technological advancements and industry-specific trends bear on business performance. Managed through an Enterprise Risk Management framework with Key Risk Indicators covering market dynamics, supply chain resilience, operational excellence, quality, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity, information security, financial controls and business continuity.
- Raw material (aluminium) price volatility — Directors' Report: aluminium and other raw material prices remained volatile due to fluctuation in the global commodity market; healthy demand conditions and the customer pass-through mechanism limited the effect on margins, so the exposure is structural and dependent on that pass-through continuing to work.
- Climate change - energy cost and regulatory pressure — BRSR material issue: high energy consumption and associated emissions from manufacturing operations expose the Group to rising energy costs and regulatory pressures; mitigation is an integrated energy management framework, energy efficiency measures, cleaner technologies, renewable energy procurement, fuel transition and process electrification.
- Emissions management and OEM decarbonisation requirements — BRSR material issue (rated Risk, financial implication Negative): increasingly stringent emissions norms, evolving carbon pricing mechanisms and heightened stakeholder expectations can materially increase compliance costs and constrain market access, particularly with global OEM customers advancing decarbonisation commitments.
- Responsible supply chain / ESG oversight of suppliers — BRSR material issue: insufficient oversight of ESG practices within the supply chain exposes the Group to reputational damage, regulatory non-compliance and operational disruptions with direct implications for OEM customers, suppliers, investors and regulators; mitigated through the Supplier Code of Conduct and an ESG-based supplier evaluation framework under development.
- Employee health and safety — BRSR material issue: unsafe or inadequately controlled working conditions can result in workplace incidents, regulatory penalties, diminished morale and reputational harm, disrupt operations and affect OEM customers who apply rigorous responsible supply chain standards; mitigated by an ISO 45001-aligned OH&S management system, safety training, risk assessments, mock drills, audits and PPE compliance.
- Waste management and environmental compliance — BRSR material issue: inadequate waste management exposes the Group to soil and water contamination, non-compliance penalties and increased disposal costs; mitigated by segregation at source and disposal through authorised recyclers.
- Workforce attrition, particularly among permanent workers — BRSR Section A item 22: turnover rate for permanent workers rose to 58.60% in FY 2025-26 from 18.69% in FY 2024-25 (25.66% in FY 2023-24), and for permanent employees to 42.72% from 40.75%. The Company also notes reliance on emerging workforce models including Fixed Term Employment, and that 4,174 of 5,980 workers are other-than-permanent.

business.body: The Rico Group is engaged in the design, development, manufacturing and supply of high-precision, engineering-grade aluminium and ferrous components and assemblies for the global automotive industry, with integrated capabilities spanning product design, tooling, casting, precision machining and assembly. It produces engine and transmission parts, braking systems and other critical components for two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles, and its product portfolio supports Hybrid Vehicles, Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Internal Combustion Engines (ICEs). Incorporated in 1983, the Group operates 16 manufacturing plants with 6,000+ employees and a presence in 4 continents, and has created a non-auto vertical focused on Railways and manufacturing of CNC machines.

business.body:
- **Casting of Non-Ferrous Metals (NIC 24320) - 88% of turnover:** Aluminium castings and machined components
- **Casting of Iron (NIC 24319) - 12% of turnover:** Ferrous castings and machined components
- **Automotive components and systems:** Engine and transmission parts, Braking systems, Structural components, System-level products, Hybrid / Electric Vehicle components, ICE vehicle components
- **Non-auto vertical:** Railways, CNC machines
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- AAN Engineering Industries Limited — subsidiary: 100% held by the listed entity. AS 9100D certified manufacturer of precision machined components and assemblies, including systems for the Aerospace, Naval and Defence industry; holds a Defence Industrial Licence for containerised shooting ranges and for ammunition manufacturing, and has signed a Transfer of Technology with TBRL (DRDO) for design and manufacture of baffle shooting ranges.
- Rico Jinfei Wheels Limited — subsidiary: Described in BRSR Section A as 'Subsidiary and JV' with 97.75% held by the Company directly or indirectly through its subsidiary; Form AOC-1 states 96.31% shareholding after the merger, being 10,59,25,000 equity shares. Material subsidiary under SEBI LODR. Has two divisions: the Wheels Division (light-weight alloy wheels for scooters, motorcycles and electric two-wheelers, developed with customers such as Hero, Bajaj and Honda) and the Pump Division (oil and water pumps for PV and CV applications) following the merger of Rico Fluidtronics Limited.
- Rico Friction Technologies Limited — subsidiary: 70% held by the listed entity; engaged in manufacturing of friction material for automotive application.
- Rico Care Foundation — subsidiary: 59.80% of paid-up capital held; Section 8 company through which the Company's CSR activities/projects are carried out, covering education, healthcare, sports, environment protection and community development; also undertakes CSR projects of Rico Group companies. Not considered for consolidation.
- Rico Auto Industries Inc., USA — subsidiary: 100% held; engaged in trading of auto components and providing warehousing, logistics and last-mile support to OEM and Tier-I customers in North America, Mexico and Brazil for goods manufactured by the Company.
- Rico Auto Industries (UK) Limited, U.K. — subsidiary: 100% held; business model changed post-Brexit, with the Company having started direct supplies to many European customers.
- Rico Fluidtronics Limited — subsidiary: Merged with and into Rico Jinfei Wheels Limited; NCLT Chandigarh approved the scheme of amalgamation by order dated 1st July 2025 with appointed date 1st April 2023. Form AOC-1 records the merger as effective 01.07.2025.
- Roop Ram Industries Private Limited — associate: 26% shareholding, held as a strategic investment to procure solar power at subsidised rates through a Power Purchase Agreement. Under the shareholders' agreement the Company has no right to Roop Ram's profit and loss and will receive back its investment at the end of the PPA term, so it is not consolidated.
- Boond Renewable Energy Private Limited — associate: 26% shareholding acquired during the year for purchase of renewable energy through a Power Purchase Agreement; same shareholders'-agreement terms as Roop Ram, hence not consolidated and not treated as an associate for BRSR/ESG purposes.
- Rasa Autocom Limited, Rico Aluminium and Ferrous Auto Components Limited, Rico Investments Limited — subsidiary: Former subsidiaries merged with Rico Auto Industries Limited with appointed date 1st April 2021; prior-year financial highlights are reinstated for the merger.

latest_quarter.body:
- Aluminium / RM prices volatile in FY26; customer pass-through "with limited effect on margins," but **lag** in quarterly settlement caused the INR19 cr FY26 drag.

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 revenue INR2,477 cr (+12%, highest ever); reported EBITDA 9% / normalized 10.25%; PAT 52.4 cr (vs 19.2). Two one-offs: Labour Code INR11 cr + RM lag INR19 cr (FY). Net debt INR686 cr (~3.75x), WC days 7 (vs 33), CFO INR331 cr. New orders INR2,500 cr/5 yrs; ~40 single-source launches. outlook.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 to **cross INR3,000 cr** (~21–25% growth off INR2,477 cr) — driven by ~40 new single-source launches, not just market growth.
- **Margin:** FY26 normalized 10.25% is "protected" (75% of customers by value agreed to monthly RM settlement); FY27 expected **above 10.25%**; 10%+ margin from Q1 FY27 onwards. Additional upside if prior-year lag-loss recovery negotiations succeed.
- **Exports:** guided to grow **~32% this year** (FY27), primarily Germany + USA; export to US/Germany to **2x over next 2 years**.
- **EV/hybrid mix:** Hosur plant (operational Sep-2026) "primarily caters to hybrid and EV-related programs" — no explicit EV revenue % target given.
- **Capex/commissioning:** Hosur facility operational from **Sep 2026**; Tamil Nadu subsidy ~INR39 cr approved, accruing from FY27 over 10 years.
- **Railways:** target to cross **INR100 cr in FY27** (vs ~INR3–4 cr FY26); **Defence** target to cross **INR50 cr** (vs ~INR20–30 cr), double over 2 yrs.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Focus on Electrification - the stated corporate strategy line under 'Customer Focussed Enterprise, Efficient Account, Program & Launch Management and Focus on Electrification'.
- Expand the business by strengthening development of system-level products, braking system competencies and structural parts.
- Explore new domestic and international markets by delivering engineering and manufacturing solutions.
- Scale the adjacent Railway and Defence businesses, utilising existing manufacturing infrastructure and engineering capabilities.
- Build the CNC machine-tool business, combining strategic sourcing of premium-grade castings and sheet metal with in-house manufacturing and quality controls.
- Drive sustainable growth through disciplined cost optimization initiatives and optimal utilization of installed capacities to enhance operational efficiency and improve profitability.
- Commission the new Hosur facility, aligned towards next-gen mobility manufacturing, to serve Toyota, AISIN and other southern-region OEMs primarily for Hybrid and EVs.
- Continually increase use of renewable energy (solar and wind) in plants to support the target of reducing carbon footprint and to save energy cost.
- Focus on return on Capital Employed and consistent dividend distribution (stated 'Stakeholder Value' strategy).
- Leverage AIoT, intelligent automation and advanced analytics to improve manufacturing efficiency, strengthen quality and enable faster, data-driven decision-making.
- The Company's stated strategy under 'Stakeholder Value' is a focus on return on Capital Employed and consistent dividend distribution. Dividend is paid in accordance with the Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy published on the Company's website; for FY 2025-26 a dividend of 55 per cent, i.e. Rs 0.55 per equity share of Rs 1 each, is placed before the 43rd AGM for declaration, and no amount was transferred to reserves during the year. Board-approved policies also govern the determination of Material Subsidiaries and Material Related Party Transactions; all contracts, arrangements and transactions with related parties during the year were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis with Audit Committee approval, and no material related party transactions were entered into, so there are no particulars to report in Form AOC-2. CSR spending is routed through Rico Care Foundation, the Group's Section 8 company.
- All manufacturing facilities within the RICO Group are certified under ISO 14001 Environmental Management System and ISO 45001 Occupational Health & Safety Management System.
- The Group has completed its Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 GHG inventory and developed a decarbonization roadmap for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.
- Named decarbonisation levers: replacement of high-carbon fuels (eliminating Furnace Oil and substituting LSHS with biodiesel), conversion of PNG-fired furnaces to electric furnaces, phased replacement of R-22 refrigerants with R-32, adoption of biodiesel and compressed biogas (CBG) blending, electrification of the corporate fleet, and increased procurement of renewable electricity.
- Renewable energy consumption increased by 41.31%, raising its share in the overall energy mix to 12.26% compared with the previous year's 8.47% (Section 134(3)(m) annexure).
- Energy intensity of operations decreased from 4.23 to 3.69 GJ per lakh of turnover, and Scope 1 GHG emissions were reduced by 16.92% versus the previous year owing to electrification of furnaces, forklifts, etc. (Section 134(3)(m) annexure).
- Green power installations in use: captive solar at Gurugram (10 MW), solar and wind at Chennai (3.5 MW), rooftop solar at Bawal (1.40 MW), at Rico Jinfei Wheels Manesar (450 KW), at Pathredi (1000 KW) and at Haridwar (500 KW).
- Strategic 26% investments in Roop Ram Industries Private Limited and Boond Renewable Energy Private Limited made solely to procure solar/renewable power at subsidised rates through Power Purchase Agreements.
- The Company is developing systems to monitor and minimise energy consumption and emission generation across its plants, implementing energy efficiency measures, cleaner technologies, renewable energy procurement, fuel transition and process electrification.
- An ESG-based supplier evaluation framework is being developed alongside adherence to the Supplier Code of Conduct, to address supply chain quality, delivery, GHG emissions and ESG compliance risks.
- Environmental Health and Safety Committees are constituted at each manufacturing location with equal representation from management and the workforce.
- Social: the RICO Medicare Centre at Pathredi provides accessible healthcare to thousands of beneficiaries annually through OPD consultations, mobile healthcare services and specialised medical camps; community initiatives support education, skill development and the empowerment of women and youth.
- Governance and disclosure: policies cover all nine NGRBC principles; the Group maintains a Vigil Mechanism/Whistle-Blower Policy, Human Rights Policy, Forced Labor and Modern Slavery Policy, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy and POSH Policy, with grievance redressal extending to all operations and stakeholders.
- Diversity: women constitute 20.00% of the Board of Directors (2 of 10) and 16.67% of Key Management Personnel (1 of 6); permanent employees are 2.09% female and permanent workers 3.16% female.
- BRSR assurance is not obtained, as the Company does not fall within the top 500 listed companies by market capitalisation and the requirement is therefore not applicable.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The headline expansion is a new greenfield plant at Hosur, listed as the Company's 2026 key milestone and shown in the Manufacturing Locations spread as an 'Upcoming Manufacturing Plant'. The Directors' Report states that readiness of the new facility at SIPCOT Industrial Park, Shoolagiri, Hosur, Tamil Nadu is in progress and that commercial production is expected to start during Q3 of the current financial year, catering to the requirements of Toyota, AISIN and other OEMs in the southern region primarily for Hybrid and EVs; the facility is described as aligned towards next-gen mobility manufacturing and is said to contribute to the Company's vision of 3X growth. The Group operates 16 manufacturing plants (16 plants and 1 office nationally per BRSR Section A), and management says the facilities are geographically spread and strategically located to de-risk operations, with various new businesses launched for optimum utilisation of existing capacities. Renewable capacity continues to be added at the plants: captive solar at Gurugram (10 MW), solar and wind at Chennai (3.5 MW), rooftop solar at Bawal (1.40 MW), at Rico Jinfei Wheels Manesar (450 KW), at Pathredi (1000 KW) and at Haridwar (500 KW). On the technology side, the Company scaled Industry 4.0 initiatives, expanding robotics, automated inspection and gauging technologies and integrated material handling systems, and IoT-enabled real-time monitoring. R&D spend for 2025-26 comprised capital expenditure of Rs 4.70 crore and operating expenditure of Rs 10.63 crore, a total of Rs 15.33 crore as printed in the Section 134(3)(m) annexure. In BRSR Principle 2 the Group reports that 0.64% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (4.11% in FY 2024-25) went into technologies improving environmental and social impact - wet scrubbers for air emissions, ETP and STP systems with RO and ultrafiltration, and natural gas detection systems - and 26.27% of R&D investment (22.28% in FY 2024-25) into such technologies. Prior expansion milestones recorded in the AR include the 2013 non-auto vertical (Railways, CNC machine manufacturing), the 2014 acquisition of a 70% stake in Rico Friction Technologies, and the earlier addition of the Bawal, Pathredi, Chennai, Halol, Bhiwadi, Sanand, Haridwar and Manesar plants.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Company anticipates good growth over the next few years driven by an increase in demand of components for Hybrid, Electric and ICE vehicles for domestic and export markets.
- The Indian Auto Component Industry will continue its strong growth trajectory and remains a key contributor to the country's manufacturing ecosystem and exports.
- The domestic clean mobility landscape is witnessing a significant shift driven by advancements in Hybrid Electric, Plug-in Hybrid, Battery Electric, Flex Fuel and Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles, which the Company expects to capitalise on by leveraging its technological expertise.
- All segments of the auto industry are expected to maintain their growth momentum in FY 2026-27; export demand is expected to remain strong, with 'Made in India' vehicles gaining increasing traction in global markets.
- New program orders and ramp-up across customers including Toyota, BMW, GKN, Maruti Suzuki, Tata, Renault, Aisin, Bosch, Cummins, Knorr-Bremse and Hero - across transmission, braking systems, engine and EV-related applications - provide good visibility and are expected to support future growth over the coming years.
- Aluminium and other raw material prices remained volatile due to fluctuation in the global commodity market; healthy demand conditions and the customer pass-through mechanism helped manage the impact with limited effect on margins.
- Railway and Defence supplies have started improving gradually and these businesses are scaling up on existing manufacturing infrastructure and engineering capabilities.
- RBI has projected India's GDP growth for FY 2026-27 at around 6.6%-6.9%, highlighting risks from external demand weakness and cost pressures faced by domestic industries.
- The Company has also secured new orders worth approximately INR 2,500 crore over a program life of 5 years, providing strong visibility for future growth.
- We also continue to strengthen our business pipeline with new program orders and ramp up across customers, including Toyota, BMW, GKN, Maruti Suzuki, Tata, Renault, Aisin, Bosch, Cummins, Knorr-Bremse and Hero - programs across transmission, braking systems, Engine and EV-related applications.
- Chairman: 'We also secured healthy order inflows across our core product portfolio spanning transmission systems, braking systems, engine components and components for electric vehicles.'
- Chairman: 'Your Company enters the new financial year with a healthy order book, a diversified customer base and a clear strategic focus on innovation, operational excellence, localisation and sustainable value creation.'

risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: evolving market conditions, global supply chain interdependencies, changing customer expectations, stringent regulatory requirements and operational risks across the manufacturing and distribution network; macroeconomic developments, geopolitical events, technological advancements and industry-specific trends bear on business performance. Managed through an Enterprise Risk Management framework with Key Risk Indicators covering market dynamics, supply chain resilience, operational excellence, quality, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity, information security, financial controls and business continuity.
risks.risk: Complex, fast-changing operating environment across manufacturing and distribution

risks.note: Directors' Report: aluminium and other raw material prices remained volatile due to fluctuation in the global commodity market; healthy demand conditions and the customer pass-through mechanism limited the effect on margins, so the exposure is structural and dependent on that pass-through continuing to work.

BRSR material issue: high energy consumption and associated emissions from manufacturing operations expose the Group to rising energy costs and regulatory pressures; mitigation is an integrated energy management framework, energy efficiency measures, cleaner technologies, renewable energy procurement, fuel transition and process electrification.
risks.risk: Climate change - energy cost and regulatory pressure

risks.note: BRSR material issue (rated Risk, financial implication Negative): increasingly stringent emissions norms, evolving carbon pricing mechanisms and heightened stakeholder expectations can materially increase compliance costs and constrain market access, particularly with global OEM customers advancing decarbonisation commitments.
risks.risk: Emissions management and OEM decarbonisation requirements

risks.note: BRSR material issue: insufficient oversight of ESG practices within the supply chain exposes the Group to reputational damage, regulatory non-compliance and operational disruptions with direct implications for OEM customers, suppliers, investors and regulators; mitigated through the Supplier Code of Conduct and an ESG-based supplier evaluation framework under development.
risks.risk: Responsible supply chain / ESG oversight of suppliers

risks.note: BRSR material issue: unsafe or inadequately controlled working conditions can result in workplace incidents, regulatory penalties, diminished morale and reputational harm, disrupt operations and affect OEM customers who apply rigorous responsible supply chain standards; mitigated by an ISO 45001-aligned OH&S management system, safety training, risk assessments, mock drills, audits and PPE compliance.

BRSR material issue: inadequate waste management exposes the Group to soil and water contamination, non-compliance penalties and increased disposal costs; mitigated by segregation at source and disposal through authorised recyclers.

BRSR Section A item 22: turnover rate for permanent workers rose to 58.60% in FY 2025-26 from 18.69% in FY 2024-25 (25.66% in FY 2023-24), and for permanent employees to 42.72% from 40.75%. The Company also notes reliance on emerging workforce models including Fixed Term Employment, and that 4,174 of 5,980 workers are other-than-permanent.
